clue.text: No taste for greens? That is disturbing

definitions.meaning: someone with no taste for putting on golf greens is put off that part of the game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' looks like vegetables, but they are golf greens, where the ball is putted.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes a golfer turned against the short game; as one word it means unsettling or repellent.

clue.text: Wild party held in Bangor gymnasium.

indicators.note: the letters are held within the run of the two words Bangor gymnasium

explanation.surface: A rowdy party has taken place inside a Welsh town's gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, unrestrained party or debauch is the classic sense of the word.

clue.text: … exhibiting Charley's relative in binge

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits inside the other here

parts.note: a fling is a spell of self-indulgent excess, a binge
Charley's Aunt is a famous Victorian farce, so Charley's relative is his aunt

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a relative of Charley during a drinking spree.
explanation.walkthrough: Charley's Aunt (1892) is a long-running English stage farce by Brandon Thomas.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaunting means displaying ostentatiously, showing off something.

clue.text: Thrown off balance in riding school

parts.note: a jockey who is riding a horse is said to be up
a set is a group or class in a school, so school can stand for set

explanation.surface: A pupil at a riding school falls off a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset means knocked over or disturbed, physically or emotionally unbalanced.

clue.text: Potential wooer, according to Rowley?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme with the refrain 'Heigh ho, says Rowley' tells of a frog who would a-wooing go, and a young frog-to-be is what is meant

explanation.walkthrough: The English nursery song 'A Frog He Would A-Wooing Go' has the refrain 'Heigh ho, says Rowley'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is the larval stage of a frog, so it could grow up to be the rhyme's suitor.

clue.text: Quantities of pain-killing drugs

definitions.meaning: drugs that deaden feeling are things that numb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means figures or amounts, and also, read as numb plus -er, agents that deaden sensation.

clue.text: Crack key to code

parts.note: F is one of the musical keys
a law code, a body of rules, gives law

explanation.surface: A cipher has been broken by finding its key.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a crack or fault in a material, a defect.

clue.text: Milky juice remaining an unknown quantity

parts.note: staying on beyond the usual time is staying late, remaining behind
in algebra x is the usual symbol for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: Some milky sap still left over is of uncertain amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex is the milky sap exuded by rubber trees and other plants.

clue.text: Restlessness of adult wrens, flying about

indicators.note: birds flying about are scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Grown-up wrens show their restlessness by flitting around.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderlust is a strong urge to travel, a restless longing to roam.

clue.text: Principal flier

definitions.meaning: a red North American songbird of that name

explanation.definitionFit: The word means chief or fundamental, and is also the name of a bright red American songbird.

clue.text: Pot plant?

parts.note: not a houseplant in a pot but the plant that gives pot, slang for cannabis

explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for marijuana, also called pot, which comes from the cannabis plant.

clue.text: Silent pictures being shown here in Scotland

parts.note: dumb is an old word for unable to speak, silent
paintings and drawings are art
a film being shown is on

explanation.surface: Silent films are being screened at a Scottish venue.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumbarton is a town on the Clyde in west-central Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a historic town in Scotland, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Opening here, now that branch has gone

definitions.text: Opening here, now that branch has gone

parts.words: Opening here, now that branch has gone
parts.note: describes a hole left in a plank of timber where a branch once grew and has dropped out

explanation.definitionFit: A hole in wood where a knot, the base of a branch, has fallen out.

clue.text: Peter out to capture side in the Southern States

indicators.note: one piece takes the other prisoner, holding it inside

parts.note: to peter out is to fade away and die
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A man called Peter goes out to seize a team in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Dixie is the traditional nickname for the southern states of the USA.

clue.text: Lingering impression of cooked tater feast?

indicators.note: food that is cooked is changed in form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A potato feast leaves a flavour in the mouth afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TATER FEAST; tater is informal for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftertaste is a taste that stays in the mouth, and figuratively a lasting impression.

clue.text: Easily broken up (accomplished after half a day)

indicators.note: after puts the skilled word after the shortened day
only half of the day named is kept, its second half dropped

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week
an accomplished person is able, skilled

explanation.surface: Something comes apart easily once it has been completed after half a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Friable means crumbly, readily reduced to small pieces.

clue.text: Smoked fish left in straw hats

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped stiff straw hat

explanation.surface: Smoked fish has been left inside some straw hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloaters are herrings that have been salted and lightly smoked.

clue.text: Old timer has main heat-source in front of face

indicators.note: in front of places the heat-source before the face

parts.note: the sun is the earth's chief source of heat
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: An old man sits with his face to the warmth of the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial is an ancient device for telling time by the shadow the sun casts.

clue.text: Firm elicits an arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the letters of elicits an in a new order

explanation.surface: A company obtains a deal through negotiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges ELICITS AN; 'Firm' looks like a company but means unyielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means not stretchy, rigid and unyielding.

clue.text: England's openers too crude to occupy our attention

parts.note: the opening two letters of the word England
gross means coarse or vulgar, crude

explanation.surface: England's opening batsmen are too unrefined to hold our interest.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the openers are the first two batsmen, hence the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To engross is to absorb fully, to hold someone's whole attention.

clue.text: Crusoe's refined sugar

indicators.note: refined sugar has been processed, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: the name Crusoe with its S, used whole as fodder

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe has a supply of white processed sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' rearranges CRUSOES, the possessive's S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Sucrose is the chemical name for ordinary cane or beet sugar.

clue.text: Tickets in quarters

definitions.meaning: small notes or tickets, from French billet

explanation.definitionFit: A billet is a ticket or short note, and also lodging assigned to troops.

clue.text: Miner, diffident follower of immaculate leader?

definitions.text: Miner, diffident follower of immaculate leader?

parts.words: Miner, diffident follower of immaculate leader?
parts.note: the seven dwarfs worked in a mine and followed Snow White, pure as snow; one of them is named for shyness

explanation.definitionFit: One of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White tale is named for being shy.

clue.text: Food & drink to someone

definitions.meaning: raise a glass in someone's honour

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both grilled bread and a salute made by raising glasses.

clue.text: Acute feeling of remorse felt in Penang Strait

indicators.note: the letters can be felt inside the run of Penang Strait

explanation.surface: Someone suffers pangs of guilt while in a Malaysian strait.
explanation.walkthrough: Penang is an island state of Malaysia.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a deep feeling of anxiety or dread, an acute inner torment.

clue.text: Get rid of Selkirk, for example

definitions.meaning: Alexander Selkirk was a sailor marooned on an island, the model for Robinson Crusoe

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it means discard; as one it is a marooned sailor such as Selkirk.

clue.text: Taking off with a high-pitched sound

parts.note: a ping is a short high ringing noise

explanation.surface: An aircraft takes off with a shrill noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' means mimicking, not an aircraft leaving the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone off is imitating them, mimicking like a monkey.

clue.text: Below ancient city, a long red river

indicators.note: below puts the following letters after the city in a down entry

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Beneath an ancient city flows a long, red-tinted river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' means Soviet, so a red river is a Russian one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural flows through Russia, and red was a byword for the Soviet Union.

clue.text: Saul go far away to find this mountain?

indicators.note: away suggests the letters are sent off in another order

explanation.surface: Saul travels a great distance to discover a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' rearranges SAUL GO FAR; Sugarloaf Mountain overlooks Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar Loaf is the name of several peaks, notably the one above Rio's harbour.

clue.text: Cold season's start not apparent in Bury

indicators.note: the opening letter of the season is not visible, so it is dropped

parts.note: winter is the cold season of the year

explanation.surface: The beginning of winter is not yet visible in a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the town near Manchester but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, to bury it.

clue.text: Common grub found in wheat-stalks

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of wheat-stalks

explanation.surface: An ordinary larva lives inside the stems of wheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like a larva but is slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, just as grub is.

clue.text: Half-sovereign reasonable for such work on rocks?

indicators.note: only half of the king's name is kept, its second half lost

parts.note: George is the name of several British sovereigns
logical means sensible, reasonable

explanation.surface: A half-sovereign coin is a fair price for some study of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-sovereign was a British gold coin worth ten shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological describes the study of the earth's rocks and their history.
